definition.name: Environmental sensor
definition.description: A powered sensor supplies a switched live output when its condition is met.

terminals.label: L
terminals.purpose: Line conductor: the alternating supply relative to neutral.

terminals.label: N
terminals.purpose: Neutral: the normal return path. It is not a protective conductor.

terminals.label: IN
terminals.purpose: Wired permission input, sensed relative to N. A connected IN path must carry sufficient input voltage before the declared condition/timer can request the output. It is not a dry-contact output.

terminals.label: OUT
terminals.purpose: Powered switched output from L. Its contact closes only when the controller is supplied and the wired permission, environmental condition and declared delay permit operation. OUT is not isolated from this controller supply.

parts.name: Housing
parts.purpose: The enclosure supports and separates functional parts. This original teaching model is representative equipment, not a manufacturer drawing.

parts.name: Removable cover
parts.purpose: The cover limits access to internal connections. Opening it here is a virtual inspection operation.

parts.name: Terminal clamps
parts.purpose: Metal clamps establish connections to individual conductors. The circuit engine connects terminal IDs, not the apparent proximity of 3D wires.

parts.name: Mounting and fixings
parts.purpose: Mounting hardware supports the equipment. Screws, rail clips and glands are modelled separately from electrical connections.

parts.name: Sensing element
parts.purpose: The sensor converts an environmental condition or measured current into a control decision. Setpoints and input values can be changed in the inspector.

parts.name: Electronic control board
parts.purpose: This conceptual board represents an electronic interface. The model follows stated input, output and power limits rather than reconstructing proprietary firmware.
